Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to youth sports development, pledging support for the growth of young table tennis talents through initiatives such as the Daniel Ford International Elite Youth Table Tennis Championship. The Governor gave the assurance while receiving a delegation led by the Managing Director of Daniel Ford International, Yemi Edun, alongside the President of ITTF Africa and Executive Vice President of the International Table Tennis Federation, Wahid Oshodi, and two emerging table tennis players, Matthew Kuti and Emmanuella Shaibu. The delegation formally invited Governor Sanwo-Olu to the grand finale of the fourth edition of the championship, scheduled to hold on December 20, 2026, at the historic Rowe Park Sports Centre, Yaba, Lagos. Recalling his attendance at the previous edition of the tournament, Governor Sanwo-Olu expressed delight at the championship’s progress and enquired about the development of the young athletes. He encouraged the players to remain focused on their goals and commended the organisers for creating opportunities that enable young Nigerians to pursue excellence through sport. “Young people need platforms that allow them to develop their talents and realise their potential,” the Governor said. The visit also provided an opportunity for the delegation to interact with members of the Flamingos, Nigeria’s national women’s U-17 football team, whose achievements continue to bring pride and recognition to the country. Speaking on the vision behind the championship, Edun said the initiative was designed to go beyond an annual tournament and serve as a sustainable platform for discovering, nurturing and preparing Nigerian players for international competition. “Our objective is to build a clear pathway for young talents to progress from grassroots development to the global stage,” Edun said. “We want every young Nigerian who watches these players compete internationally to believe that they too can achieve similar success through dedication, hard work and opportunity.” According to Edun, the championship also seeks to inspire more children to embrace table tennis, build confidence through sport and develop the mindset needed to compete at the highest levels.
